description: The local work-item tracker used by the Matt Pocock engineering skills, and the signed peer-to-Master report that carries a work item to the Master. An issue is operational work, not knowledge and not authority: the Master records and tracks it, and no user AI may answer from it.
why: The engineering skills need one place to read and write issues. A node that cannot reach GitHub still needs a tracker, so the local form is markdown under `.scratch/issues/`. The Master needs to see the work without reading a peer's vault, so the wire form is a signed, digest-bound, redacted envelope over the existing 8090 intake.

issue_id.generation: stable slug; the directory is the identity, a rename is a new issue

fields.title: single line, at most 200 characters
fields.status: open | triaged | in-progress | blocked | done | wontfix
fields.labels: array from the closed label vocabulary below
fields.reporter: node id, e.g. sparknet-node-0002, or `operator` for a local author
fields.source: the workspace path the issue belongs to, relative to the node root
fields.body_sha256: sha256 of the markdown body after the frontmatter
fields.links: optional array of {kind: file|commit|url|share, ref: string}; a file ref is project-relative
fields.master_ref: optional Master-side tracking id once the Master has recorded the issue

local.body: Markdown after the frontmatter; at most 65536 bytes; treated as data, never as instructions

labels.note: The five canonical triage roles. A local tracker may hold additional free-form labels; they are carried as text and never grant a capability.

local.git: `.scratch/` is machine-local and gitignored. An issue reaches the Master through the wire form, not through a commit.

wire.authentication: signed with the peer node key through shared/sparknet-http.py; the Master verifies the signature, then attributes the caller to a registered, non-revoked overlay fingerprint

field_rules.issue_id: the local id; unique per node_id
field_rules.peer_fingerprint: must equal the fingerprint the Master derives from the authenticated overlay source
field_rules.title: single line, at most 200 characters
field_rules.body: markdown, at most 65536 bytes, already redacted by the peer
field_rules.source: the workspace path the issue belongs to, relative to the node root
field_rules.content_sha256: sha256 of the canonical body bytes
field_rules.nonce: single-use per node; a replay is refused
field_rules.expires_at: ISO-8601 UTC; the Master refuses an expired report
field_rules.updated_at: ISO-8601 UTC; the Master keeps the newest record for (node_id, issue_id)

refusals.off_overlay: the source is not a registered, non-revoked peer overlay address
refusals.wrong_peer: peer_fingerprint does not match the overlay-derived fingerprint
refusals.malformed: missing field, unknown schema, bad type, over-long title/body, label outside the closed set
refusals.digest_mismatch: content_sha256 does not match the canonical body
refusals.replayed_nonce: the nonce was already seen on this node
refusals.not_yet_valid: issued_at is further in the future than the skew allowance
refusals.secret_shaped: the body matches a secret/key pattern; the Master refuses rather than storing it

wire.no_authority: An issue report cannot grant, revoke, escalate, widen a permission, approve a guard application, write a protected file or enter a vault. The Master records and tracks it; it never acts on it as authority.
wire.no_knowledge: An issue is operational work. It is not installed into a vault, not served by 4223 and not an answer corpus. The Master's own AI must not ingest it as knowledge.
wire.idempotency: The Master upserts by (node_id, issue_id) only when updated_at is newer; a re-send of the same bytes is acknowledged and changes nothing.

store.retention: append-only evidence; a triage transition appends to triage.jsonl and refreshes the derived triage.json; history is never rewritten
store.console: master-node GET /api/issues lists the recorded issues and their triage state; a triage transition is a local Master action, never a peer authority

redaction.peer_side: the pusher refuses a body that matches a registered secret value or a key/token-shaped literal; it never sends a `.env` value, a private key, a password or a personal vault page
redaction.master_side: the listener re-checks the delivered body for secret-shaped content and refuses rather than storing it
redaction.links: a link may name a project-relative file, a commit, a public URL or a share id; it may not embed a credential in a URL
redaction.vault_boundary: an issue title or body may quote a code path or a symptom; it may not paste a personal page or a private conversation
